module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjectures associated with A109845

$a(1) = 2$; $a(2n)$ = lcm of all previous terms + 1; $a(2n+1)$ = lcm of all previous terms - 1.

*References:*
- [A109845](https://oeis.org/A109845)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace OeisA109845

/--
$a(1) = 2$; $a(2n)$ = lcm of all previous terms + 1; $a(2n+1)$ = lcm of all previous terms - 1.
The sequence is correctly generated by the recurrence relation $a(1)=2$, $a(2)=3$,
and for $n \ge 3$:
$$a(n) = a(n-1)^2 + (-1)^n a(n-1) + (-1)^n.$$
We use $0$-based indexing here, so $a(n)$ corresponds to the OEIS sequence $a(n+1)$.
-/
def a : ℕ → ℕ
  | 0 => 2
  | 1 => 3
  | n + 2 =>
    let prev := a (n + 1)
    if n % 2 = 0 then
      prev * prev - (prev + 1)
    else
      prev * prev + prev + 1

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_0 : a 0 = 2 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_1 : a 1 = 3 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : a 2 = 5 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : a 3 = 31 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_4 : a 4 = 929 := by rfl

/--
Conjecture: There are infinitely many primes in this sequence.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture : Set.Infinite {n : ℕ | (a n).Prime} := by
  sorry

end OeisA109845

reformulations.difference: Uses a zero-based, parity-split quadratic recurrence rather than the entry's headline definition using the lcm of all preceding terms.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: OEIS explicitly supplies this equivalent quadratic recurrence in its FORMULA section. In the lcm definition, each new term is congruent to ±1 modulo every earlier term, so the terms are pairwise coprime and each prefix lcm equals its product. Writing b(k) for the one-based sequence then gives b(k+1)=b(k)^2+(-1)^(k+1)b(k)+(-1)^(k+1) for k≥2. Lean's a(n+2) corresponds to b(n+3), so its even-n branch correctly subtracts the previous term and 1. Both initial values agree. The natural-number subtraction is harmless: its previous term is always at least 3, and the subtrahend never exceeds the square; this bound was proved in the scratch file.

reformulations.difference: States infinitude of indices whose terms are prime, rather than explicitly forming the set of distinct prime values in the sequence.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Proved StrictMono a in /workspace/review/scratch.lean without using the conjecture. Consequently a is injective, and its image on {n | (a n).Prime} is exactly {p | p.Prime ∧ p ∈ Set.range a}. Set.infinite_image_iff then proves the equivalence between the submitted statement and infinitude of the distinct prime values. The equivalence theorem's axioms contain no sorryAx.

review.notes: Checked the definition, all five test theorems, and the conjecture. All 13 terms in the published b-file matched the Lean sequence after the documented index shift; direct evaluation also confirmed the original lcm rule through those terms. Scratch proofs establish lower bounds, subtraction safety, strict monotonicity, and the prime-index/prime-value equivalence. The full OEIS entry explicitly says, "Conjecture: There are infinitely many primes in this sequence," with no recorded resolution, consistent with research open. The main OEIS entry was Cloudflare-blocked, so its full text was read from the official OEIS data mirror; the b-file was accessible directly. All experiments are under /workspace/review/.
